definitions.gloss: to drive back; to send away; to chase off
definitions.explanation: To force someone to leave or go back, often by refusing them entry or driving them away.

examples.japanese: セールスマンを{追|お}い{返|かえ}す。
{野良猫|のらねこ}を{追|お}い{返|かえ}した。
examples.english: I chased the stray cat away.

examples.japanese: {門|もん}の{前|まえ}で{不審者|ふしんしゃ}を{追|お}い{返|かえ}した。
examples.english: I drove a suspicious person away at the gate.

notes:
{追|お}い{返|かえ}す is a compound verb from {追|お}う (to chase) + {返|かえ}す (to return/send back). It means to forcefully make someone leave or go back.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pattern: [person]を{追|お}い{返|かえ}す

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- セールスマンを{追|お}い{返|かえ}す: to turn away a salesman
- {敵|てき}を{追|お}い{返|かえ}す: to drive back the enemy
- {不審者|ふしんしゃ}を{追|お}い{返|かえ}す: to chase off a suspicious person
- {野良猫|のらねこ}を{追|お}い{返|かえ}す: to chase away a stray cat

SIMILAR {追|お}い～ COMPOUNDS:
- {追|お}い{出|だ}す: to kick out, to expel (stronger)
- {追|お}い{払|はら}う: to drive away, to shoo
- {追|お}いかける: to chase after

NUANCE:
{追|お}い{返|かえ}す implies sending someone back to where they came from. {追|お}い{出|だ}す is stronger and means expelling someone entirely. {追|お}い{払|はら}う focuses on shooing or brushing away.
